Banchan / Heritage

Oi Sobagi Cucumber Kimchi

Oi sobagi is the kimchi of one afternoon: cucumbers stuffed with the kimchi paste, ready by dinner and gone by the weekend.

Korean · Easy · Makes about 800 g (a small jar, eaten within the week)

Jump to recipe ↓
Chapter 03 / 25 banchan recipes ↗

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: heritage — the summer day's kimchi. Oi sobagi is the kimchi of one afternoon: cucumbers stuffed with the kimchi paste, ready by dinner and gone by the weekend. Where the cabbage jar (#B01) runs a month's arc, cucumber kimchi runs three days — it has no long-ferment ambition, because cucumber's water works fast in both directions. This is the bowl to make the morning of a summer grill, the cold crunch against the pork records' (#M10, #M11) richness.

The cucumbers and salt
The stuffing paste

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • Cut the pockets, not through. Each cucumber is quartered lengthwise the careful way: knife down from the top, stopping 2 cm short of the end, twice in a cross — so each cucumber opens into four connected fingers, a pocket for the stuffing. The uncut end holds it all together.
  • Salt 30 minutes in cold water with the salt dissolved, weighted lightly; the cucumbers bend a half-step and weep. Rinse and drain well — a wet cucumber waters the paste down to a sauce.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    Build the stuffing: gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, ginger, sugar worked to a paste, then the scallion, chives, radish matchsticks and sesame folded through so it holds together as a coarse stuffing rather than a slurry. Checkpoint — taste a matchstick: full kimchi register, slightly stronger than you want to eat — the cucumber will dilute it over the hours.
  2. 02
    Open each cucumber's fingers and press the stuffing into the pocket and between every finger, a generous teaspoon's worth; close, roll lightly in the bowl's remaining paste. Checkpoint — each cucumber is visibly stuffed, red in the seams, green at the shoulders.
  3. 03
    Pack snugly in a container, lid on, refrigerate. Ready at 6 hours, best at 24. Checkpoint — the day-of taste: cold snap, the stuffing's salt-heat in the seams, a barely-started sourness. By day two the sourness is present; by day three the cucumbers are softening — the bowl's honest end. Chef’s Note — oi sobagi is the kimchi that teaches fermentation's honest limits: cabbage and radish are vegetables built to hold (dense, low water, high structure), cucumber is built to be eaten (watery, quick, generous) — and pretending otherwise is how good cucumbers become compost. Make it small, eat it fast, and make it again next week; that rhythm, not the jar, is the tradition.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Stuffing washed out, bland seamsWet cucumbers at stuffingDrain thoroughly after the salt rinse
Cucumbers soft by day twoOver-fermented or over-salted24-hour sweet spot; fridge from hour one
Snap never cameSkipped the salt restThe 30-minute brine bends and firms them
Pocket tore openQuartered all the way throughStop the knife 2 cm from the end

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • Refrigerated, at its best days 1–2, over by day 4 — this is a small-batch, same-week bowl by design.
  • Variations: the month-scale jars (#B01, #B02) for the long arc; the instant unfermented cucumber lane is oi muchim (#B07); the stuffing doubles inside whole radish wedges for a same-day kkakdugi cousin.
